DEFINITION · qeva:1:complex-number@2

Complex number

Complex numbers can be constructed as ordered pairs of reals with explicit field operations.

editorialanalysis · algebra
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Represent a complex number by a pair of real coordinates and define arithmetic so that the second coordinate behaves like a square root of minus one.

EXACT

The compact statement

Let C=R×R with componentwise equality, (a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d), and (a,b)·(c,d)=(ac−bd,ad+bc). Define 0_C=(0,0), 1_C=(1,0), and i=(0,1). Then i²=(-1,0), identified with the embedded real number -1.

Example

3+2i corresponds to (3,2), and (0,1)·(0,1)=(-1,0).

Boundary / caveat

The displayed operations define the construction; the field laws and uniqueness up to suitable isomorphism are separate theorems.

Assumptions

  • The complete ordered field of real numbers is fixed. · Real number @1
